simple.meaning: שָׂפָם (sâphâm) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “the beard (as a lip-piece ).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Leviticus 13:45. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׂפָם (H8222) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: שָׂפָם (sâphâm) / H8222 is traced through Leviticus 13:45, 2 Samuel 19:25, Ezekiel 24:17, Ezekiel 24:22 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H8222. sapham שָׂפָם noun [masculine] moustache (compare N Syriac rete ; on meaning and form see Thes Ol 408 Kö ii. 73 ); — absolute ׳שׂ Micah 3:7 +, suffix שְׂפָמוֺ 2Sam 19:25 ; — moustache: שׂ ׳עָשָׂה 19:25 ( ᵐ5 μύστάξ ) i.e. trim it; עַלשֿׂ ׳עָטָה Micah 3:7 ; Ezek 24:17 , 22 ; Lev 13:45 (P; see I. עטה 1 ). שִׂמַּח see III. ספח . מִשְׂמָּח see II. ספח . ִשׂפְמוֺת 1Sam 30:28 see ׳שִׁפ . שׂפן see ספן . I. שֶׂ֫פֶק שׂפק, see ספק .

occurrences.englishText: “The leper in whom the plague is shall wear torn clothes, and the hair of his head shall hang loose. He shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’
When he had come to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, “Why didn’t you go with me, Mephibosheth?”
Sigh, but not aloud. Make no mourning for the dead. Bind your headdress on you, and put your sandals on your feet. Don’t cover your lips, and don’t eat mourner’s bread.”
You will do as I have done. You won’t cover your lips or eat mourner’s bread.
